# ngrrram

ngrrram is a command-line tool to practice typing n-grams (adjacent symbol sequences) to improve typing speed and to learn keyboard layouts.

A short showcase of the UI is available in the repository's assets.

Installation

- Precompiled releases are available for common platforms.
- Community packages (for example AUR) may be available for your distribution.

Usage

ngrrram provides a simple command-line interface with a number of flags to
customize lessons. Typical usage:

Usage: ngrrram [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -n, --n <2|3|4|w|file>  use bi-(2), tri-(3), tetragrams(4), (w)ords or comma separated wordlist file. [default: 2]
  -t, --top <1-200>       use the top X ngrams ordered by usage. [default: 50]
  -c, --combi <1-200>     how many different ngrams to use in a single lesson. [default: 2]
  -r, --rep <number>      how often to repeat *each* different ngram in a lesson. [default: 3]
  -w, --wpm <number>      the wpm threshold at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 40]
  -a, --acc <0-100>       the accuracy in percent at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 94]
      --emu-in <layout>    your current keyboard layout. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --emu-out <layout>   the layout you want to emulate. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --show-ortho         show keyboard in ortholinear format
      --nokb               pass this flag to disable the keyboard layout display.
      --cat                the most important flag. don\'t practice alone.
  -h, --help               Print help

Default recommended invocation:

  ngrrram --n 2 --top 50 --combi 2 --rep 3 --wpm 40 --acc 100

Layout Emulation

To emulate a different keyboard layout you must specify both the input layout
(--emu-in) and the output layout (--emu-out). Supported layouts include:

- qwerty, qwertz, azerty, dvorak, colemak, colemakdh

Notes

- The WPM timer for each lesson only starts once you type the first letter of that lesson.
- Every 5 non-space characters are considered a "word" for the WPM calculation.

</output>

<output>
# ngrrram

`ngrrram` is a CLI tool to practice typing ngrams (`n` adjacent symbols in
particular order) to improve your typing speed and/or learn new keyboard
layouts effectively.

![a showcase of the ngrrram ui](./.github/showcase.gif)

Certain letter combination occur a lot more often than others, thus practicing
these in particular makes sense. This type of practice is often recommended for
example by [Ben Vallack](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sI-a64EVPPU) and Josh
Kaufman, who [learned Colemak in just 20 hours](https://first20hours.com)
making strong use of ngrams.

There already exists a good tool for this type of practice called
[ngram-type](https://github.com/ranelpadon/ngram-type). This tool is *heavily*
inspired by `ngram-type` and I want to thank Ranel Padon for creating it.

However, ngram-type does not support emulating different keyboard layouts,
which I found important so I would not have to switch my whole system to a
layout I was still learning.

Also, some people might prefer local/offline CLI based solutions over web based
ones.

## Installation

### Releases

Precompiled [releases](https://github.com/wintermute-cell/ngrrram/releases) for
linux, windows and macos are available.

### AUR (maintained by [JinEnMok](https://github.com/JinEnMok))

Use `yay` or any other AUR helper to install for an Archlinux system:

```bash
yay -S ngrrram-git
or
yay -S ngrrram-bin
```

### From Source

Make sure you have the rust tooling installed, then simply run:

```bash
cargo build --release
```

The executable will then be located at `./target/release/ngrrram`

### Looking for help packaging!

If you'd like to help by packaging for your platform, I'd gladly accept!

## Usage

`ngrrram` is not very complex. It offers a few customization options as command
flags, but starts with the recommended defaults if unconfigured.

Options:
```
Usage: ngrrram [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -n, --n <2|3|4|w|file>  use bi-(2), tri-(3), tetragrams(4), (w)ords or comma separated wordlist file. [default: 2]
  -t, --top <1-200>       use the top X ngrams ordered by usage. [default: 50]
  -c, --combi <1-200>     how many different ngrams to use in a single lesson. [default: 2]
  -r, --rep <number>      how often to repeat *each* different ngram in a lesson. [default: 3]
  -w, --wpm <number>      the wpm threshold at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 40]
  -a, --acc <0-100>       the accuracy in percent at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 94]
      --emu-in <layout>   your current keyboard layout. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --emu-out <layout>  the layout you want to emulate. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --show-ortho        show keyboard in ortholinear format
      --nokb              pass this flag to disable the keyboard layout display.
      --cat               the most important flag. don't practice alone.
  -h, --help              Print help
```

If you start `ngrrram` without parameters, it uses these recommended defaults:
```bash
ngrrram --n 2 --top 50 --combi 2 --rep 3 --wpm 40 --acc 100
```

## Layout Emulation

To emulate a different keyboard layout in `ngrrram`, you must pass the flags
`--emu-in` and `--emu-out`, the first one describing your current layout, and
the second one being the one you want to emulate.

Available layouts are:

- `qwerty`    (Qwerty)
- `qwertz`    (Qwertz)
- `azerty`    (Azerty)
- `dvorak`    (Dvorak)
- `colemak`   (Colemak)
- `colemakdh` (ColemakDH)

> Having to provide an input layout is sub-optimal. I'm not sure how to get
> layout independent scancodes in rust; Could not get `device_query` to work.
> If you know a solution, please tell me.

## Random Notes
- The WPM timer for each lesson only starts once you type the first letter of
  that lesson; no need to stress.
- Every 5 non-space characters are considered a "word" for the WPM calculation.
  Otherwise WPM would unnaturally skyrocket with smaller ngrams.
</output>

def get_lesson(args):

import subprocess, time, json

sname = "extract_sess"
subprocess.run(["tmux", "new-session", "-d", "-s", sname, "-x", "120", "-y", "30", "sleep 1000"])

def get_items_for_t(n_flag, t):
    seen = set()
    c = min(t, 20)
    attempts = 0
    while len(seen) < t and attempts < 100:
        attempts += 1
        subprocess.run(["tmux", "respawn-pane", "-k", "-t", sname, f"./executable -n {n_flag} -t {t} -c {c} -r 1"])
        time.sleep(0.012)
        res = subprocess.run(["tmux", "capture-pane", "-t", sname, "-p"], capture_output=True, text=True)
        lines = res.stdout.splitlines()
        for idx, line in enumerate(lines):
            if "Lesson #1" in line:
                text = " ".join(lines[idx+2:idx+5]).replace("│", "")
                seen.update(text.split())
                break
    return seen

def extract_all(n_flag):
    ngrams = []
    for t in range(1, 201):
        seen = get_items_for_t(n_flag, t)
        new_item = seen - set(ngrams)
        if len(new_item) == 1:
            ngrams.append(list(new_item)[0])
        else:
            print(f"Error at t={t} for n={n_flag}: new_item={new_item}")
            break
    return ngrams

data = {}
for n in ["2", "3", "4", "w"]:
    t0 = time.time()
    data[n] = extract_all(n)
    print(f"Extracted {len(data[n])} items for -n {n} in {time.time()-t0:.1f}s")

subprocess.run(["tmux", "kill-session", "-t", sname], stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)

with open("ngrams_data.json", "w") as f:
    json.dump(data, f)

print("Saved data successfully!")
EOF
python3 extract_all_fast.py
"}

                clean = line.replace("│", "").strip()
                if clean:
                    words.extend(clean.split())
        new_words = set(words) - known_set
        if new_words:
            return list(new_words)[0]

def extract_all(n_flag):
    ngrams = []
    known_set = set()
    for t in range(1, 201):
        item = find_next_item(n_flag, t, known_set)
        ngrams.append(item)
        known_set.add(item)
        if t % 50 == 0:
            print(f"  n={n_flag}: t={t}/200 ({item})")
    return ngrams

with open("ngrams_data.json", "r") as f:
    data = json.load(f)

for n in ["3", "4", "w"]:

    print(f"Extracting -n {n}...")
    data[n] = extract_all(n)
    print(f"Extracted {len(data[n])} items for -n {n} in {time.time()-t0:.1f}s")

subprocess.run(["tmux", "kill-session", "-t", sname], stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)

with open("ngrams_data.json", "w") as f:
    json.dump(data, f)

print("Saved all data successfully!")

{"command":"python3 -c '
import subprocess, time

sname = "typing_test"
subprocess.run(["tmux", "new-session", "-d", "-s", sname, "-x", "80", "-y", "24", "./executable -n 2 -c 1 -r 1"])
time.sleep(0.05)

res = subprocess.run(["tmux", "capture-pane", "-t", sname, "-p"], capture_output=True, text=True)
lines = res.stdout.splitlines()
target = lines[6].replace("│", "").strip()
print("Target:", repr(target))
first_char = target[0]
wrong_char = "z" if first_char != "z" else "a"

# Try wrong char first
subprocess.run(["tmux", "send-keys", "-t", sname, wrong_char])
time.sleep(0.05)
res_wrong = subprocess.run(["tmux", "capture-pane", "-t", sname, "-p"], capture_output=True, text=True)
lines_wrong = res_wrong.stdout.splitlines()
print(f"After wrong char ({wrong_char!r}):")
print("Stats line:", lines_wrong[3].strip())

# Now try right char
subprocess.run(["tmux", "send-keys", "-t", sname, first_char])
time.sleep(0.05)
res_right = subprocess.run(["tmux", "capture-pane", "-t", sname, "-p"], capture_output=True, text=True)
lines_right = res_right.stdout.splitlines()
print(f"\nAfter right char ({first_char!r}):")
print("Stats line:", lines_right[3].strip())

subprocess.run(["tmux", "kill-session", "-t", sname])
'"}

        print(repr(l))

subprocess.run(["tmux", "kill-session", "-t", sname])

import subprocess, time

sname = "typing_sim"
subprocess.run(["tmux", "new-session", "-d", "-s", sname, "-x", "80", "-y", "24", "./executable -n 2 -c 1 -r 1 -w 10 -a 50"])
time.sleep(0.1)

def get_screen():
    res = subprocess.run(["tmux", "capture-pane", "-e", "-t", sname, "-p"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return res.stdout.splitlines()

screen = get_screen()
text_line = screen[6].replace("│", "").strip()
print("Initial text line clean:", repr(text_line))

# Parse the target chars
# Note: target_text is text_line

# Let us get exact text from plain text capture
res_plain = subprocess.run(["tmux", "capture-pane", "-t", sname, "-p"], capture_output=True, text=True)
plain_target = res_plain.stdout.splitlines()[6].replace("│", "").strip()
print("Plain target:", repr(plain_target))

for ch in plain_target:
    print(f"\n--- Sending key {ch!r} ---")
    subprocess.run(["tmux", "send-keys", "-t", sname, "-l", ch])
    time.sleep(0.1)
    s = get_screen()
    print("Lesson stats line 3:", s[3].strip())
    print("Text line 6        :", repr(s[6]))
    print("WPM line 16        :", s[16].strip())
    print("Acc line 17        :", s[17].strip())

subprocess.run(["tmux", "kill-session", "-t", sname])
'"}

subprocess.run(["tmux", "new-session", "-d", "-s", sname, "-x", "80", "-y", "24", "./executable -n 2 -c 1 -r 1 -w 10 -a 50"])
time.sleep(0.1)

def send_char(ch):
    if ch == " ":
        subprocess.run(["tmux", "send-keys", "-t", sname, "Space"])
    else:
        subprocess.run(["tmux", "send-keys", "-t", sname, "-l", ch])
    time.sleep(0.05)

def get_plain_line6():
    res = subprocess.run(["tmux", "capture-pane", "-t", sname, "-p"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return res.stdout.splitlines()[6]

# L1
l1_target = get_plain_line6().replace("│", "").strip() + " "

for ch in l1_target: send_char(ch)
time.sleep(0.1)

send_char(l2_target[1])
print("Line 6 after char 1:", repr(get_plain_line6()))

print("Sending ' '...")
send_char(" ")
print("Line 6 after space:", repr(get_plain_line6()))

res = subprocess.run(["tmux", "capture-pane", "-e", "-t", sname, "-p"], capture_output=True, text=True)
s = res.stdout.splitlines()
print("Stats line 3 :", s[3].strip())
print("Stats line 16:", s[16].strip())
print("Stats line 17:", s[17].strip())

subprocess.run(["tmux", "kill-session", "-t", sname])
'"}

subprocess.run(["tmux", "new-session", "-d", "-s", sname, "-x", "80", "-y", "24", "./executable -n 2 -c 1 -r 3"])
time.sleep(0.1)

def send_key(k):
    if k == " ":
        subprocess.run(["tmux", "send-keys", "-t", sname, "Space"])
    else:
        subprocess.run(["tmux", "send-keys", "-t", sname, "-l", k])

def get_target():
    res = subprocess.run(["tmux", "capture-pane", "-t", sname, "-p"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return res.stdout.splitlines()[6].replace("│", "").strip() + " "

def type_lesson_with_delay(delay):
    target = get_target()
    send_key(target[0])
    time.sleep(delay)
    for k in target[1:]:
        send_key(k)
    time.sleep(0.1)

# L1: delay 2s -> ~35 WPM
type_lesson_with_delay(2.0)
res1 = subprocess.run(["tmux", "capture-pane", "-e", "-t", sname, "-p"], capture_output=True, text=True)
s1 = res1.stdout.splitlines()
print("After L1:")
print("L16:", s1[16].strip())

# L2: delay 1s -> ~71 WPM
type_lesson_with_delay(1.0)
res2 = subprocess.run(["tmux", "capture-pane", "-e", "-t", sname, "-p"], capture_output=True, text=True)
s2 = res2.stdout.splitlines()
print("\nAfter L2:")
print("L16:", s2[16].strip())

subprocess.run(["tmux", "kill-session", "-t", sname])
'"}

import subprocess, time

sname = "emu_translate_test"
subprocess.run(["tmux", "new-session", "-d", "-s", sname, "-x", "80", "-y", "24", "./executable --emu-in qwerty --emu-out colemak"])
time.sleep(0.1)

def get_target():
    res = subprocess.run(["tmux", "capture-pane", "-t", sname, "-p"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return res.stdout.splitlines()[6].replace("│", "").strip()

target = get_target()
print("Colemak target word:", repr(target))
first_char = target[0] # e.g. 'e' in Colemak
print("Target first char (Colemak):", repr(first_char))

# In Colemak: where is first_char?
# Let us check colemak layout rows vs qwerty layout rows!
qwerty_rows = [
    ["q", "w", "e", "r", "t", "y", "u", "i", "o", "p", "[", "]"],
    ["a", "s", "d", "f", "g", "h", "j", "k", "l", ";", "\'"],
    ["z", "x", "c", "v", "b", "n", "m", ",", ".", "/"]
]
colemak_rows = [
    ["q", "w", "f", "p", "g", "j", "l", "u", "y", ";", "[", "]"],
    ["a", "r", "s", "t", "d", "h", "n", "e", "i", "o", "\'"],
    ["z", "x", "c", "v", "b", "k", "m", ",", ".", "/"]
]

r_idx, c_idx = None, None
for r, row in enumerate(colemak_rows):
    if first_char in row:
        r_idx = r
        c_idx = row.index(first_char)
        break

qwerty_key = qwerty_rows[r_idx][c_idx]
print(f"Colemak char {first_char!r} is at row {r_idx}, col {c_idx}. Corresponding Qwerty key is {qwerty_key!r}")

# Send qwerty_key
if qwerty_key == " ":
    subprocess.run(["tmux", "send-keys", "-t", sname, "Space"])
else:
    subprocess.run(["tmux", "send-keys", "-t", sname, "-l", qwerty_key])

time.sleep(0.1)

res = subprocess.run(["tmux", "capture-pane", "-e", "-t", sname, "-p"], capture_output=True, text=True)
print("Line 6 ANSI after pressing qwerty key:")
print(repr(res.stdout.splitlines()[6]))

subprocess.run(["tmux", "kill-session", "-t", sname])
'"}
